newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Shareholder row at Russian copper smelter - paper.
newsitem.headline: Shareholder row at Russian copper smelter - paper.

text.p: A major Russian shareholder in the Urals-based Sredneuralsk (SUMZ) copper smelter wants to loosen the grip of another shareholder, Swiss trading giant Glencore AG, on plant policy, Kommersant Daily said on Thursday.

The newspaper said that Ekologiya, a Moscow-based firm controlling 42 percent of the plant, was unhappy about the way Glencore was running the business, signalling another shareholder spat in Russia's non-ferrous metals industry.
But Glencore, which with its partners owns 56 percent of the plant's shares, was making deals which make perfect commercial sense, the paper quoted the plant's highest official as saying.
"There is not enough Russian copper concentrate to meet Urals' demands," SUMZ general director Nikita Novikov said.
Glencore in Moscow declined to comment.
The plant's capacity is 132,000 tonnes a year, but it is producing well below that level.
Glencore supplies it with copper concentrate from Mongolia's giant Erdenet mine.
